about: The era registry (docs/data-plan.md, section 1). An era is a period in one environment in which nothing that affects play changed. Eras before build stamps are defined by environment and UTC window (from inclusive, to exclusive; to null while the era runs), plus layout and mindVersion (null: the facts carry none); stamped eras by `build` (set at deploy by scripts/deploy.mjs as <env>-<YYYY-MM-DD>-<short sha>[-dirty]). At each deploy: close the running era of that environment (`to`), and add or fill the new one (`build`, `from`, worker, commits). Predictions are judged by scripts/era-report.mjs against the era's `baseline` (see scripts/lib/eras.mjs for the measures and verdict rules). Times come from `wrangler deployments list`.

eras.change: The lighter Jev (L4, mindVersion 6): a bot decides only at decision moments (it spawns, its goal ends or fails, the case changes state, or 10 s pass) and holds its goal in between; Jev is asked at those moments, never within 3 s of the last request; each decision also sets a stance, fight or focus (ignore rats unless they block the way or shoot). Every decision moment is recorded with its stance. About 1 round in 5 is a code-only round: the bots keep the code mind even with humans playing, to measure what Jev is worth. Ships with protocol 25 (Tyler, 30 September): Closing Time dropped (three modes), Blackout with a hard flashlight beam on every rat, heavy Big Cheese (one shot per second, damage 2 plus one per size step).
eras.notes: Jev, decision and human-likeness measures and these verdicts read ordinary rounds only; the report compares code-only rounds with ordinary ones in their own section. Production's bot overhaul era measured 56 requests per bot-minute (bots counted from the frames, about 7 in the room); the plan's 48 matches about 9 bots. The bound of 12 stands either way. Protocol 25 changes modes and two incidents in the same era: compare per mode, and read Big Cheese and Blackout rounds apart (Big Cheese cuts shots per minute by design). Staging: build staging-2026-10-01-1a9af7b (Worker a872995f), rolling only Blackout and Big Cheese for Tyler's playtest.

predictions.says: Jev requests per bot-minute fall from about 48 to under 12.
Dollars per hour Jev is on fall at least fivefold.
The share of take-the-case goals replaced before they end falls well below 89%.
Human-likeness gets no worse: the gap between bot and human hit rates across distance bands does not grow.
Human-likeness gets no worse: the gap between the bots' and the humans' share of shots fired with no rat in sight does not grow.
